`OpenVireoRustCore` is the Swift binding of the core: accounts, vaults, sync, share links and `.kdbx`
files, on the same Rust code as the iOS, desktop and web apps. UniFFI generates the Swift API from
[`bindings/ov-ffi`](https://github.com/openvireo/openvireo-core/tree/v1.2.2/bindings/ov-ffi) over `OpenVireoCore.xcframework`, which holds the core as static
libraries for iOS, the iOS simulator and macOS.

- iOS 15 or later and macOS 12 or later, Swift 5.9 or later (Xcode 15+).
- Every call that touches the network or storage is `async` and takes a `CancelToken`.
- The app supplies the Host (HTTP, secure store, offline cache, clock, log sink), so TLS, the Keychain
  and logging stay on Apple's APIs.

## Install

The package is [openvireo-swift](https://github.com/openvireo/openvireo-swift). Each core release updates it
and tags the same version, without the `v`: `1.2.0` there is core `v1.2.0`.

In Xcode: **File → Add Package Dependencies…**, enter `https://github.com/openvireo/openvireo-swift`, and
add the `OpenVireoRustCore` library to your app target.

In `Package.swift`:

```swift
dependencies: [
    .package(url: "https://github.com/openvireo/openvireo-swift", from: "1.2.2"),
],
targets: [
    .target(name: "MyApp", dependencies: [
        .product(name: "OpenVireoRustCore", package: "openvireo-swift"),
    ]),
]
```

SwiftPM downloads the xcframework from the core's GitHub release and checks it against the checksum in the
package's `Package.swift`. The same zip is in the release's `SHA256SUMS`, which is signed by the
[OpenVireo release key](https://openvireo.com/verifying-signatures).

Check the install:

```swift
import OpenVireoRustCore

print(OpenVireoRustCore.version())   // 1.2.2
```

Qualify `Host` and `version()` as `OpenVireoRustCore.Host` and `OpenVireoRustCore.version()` where
Foundation or XCTest has a member of the same name.

## A client

An `OvClient` needs a `ClientConfig` (this device) and a `Host`. The Host is five protocols you implement:
`HttpTransport`, `SecureStore`, `BlobCache`, `Clock` and `LogSink`.
[`Host.swift`](https://github.com/openvireo/openvireo-examples-swift/blob/main/Sources/Examples/Host.swift) in
the examples is a small one on Foundation (URLSession with no redirects and no cookies, memory for the store
and the cache). An app keeps the store in the Keychain and the cache on disk, so vaults open offline.

```swift
import OpenVireoRustCore

let host = OpenVireoRustCore.Host(
    http: URLSessionTransport(), store: KeychainStore(), cache: DiskCache(), clock: SystemClock(), log: OSLogSink())
let client = OvClient(
    config: ClientConfig(device: DeviceInfo(id: nil, name: "My app", platform: .ios), offline: true, server: nil),
    host: host)
```

- `device.name` is what the account's device list shows.
- `offline: true` keeps the offline cache: unlock, list and open vaults without the network, and keep edits
  until they upload.
- `server` is a discovery document to use instead of fetching one. Leave it `nil`.

## Sign in and read a field

```swift
let cancel = CancelToken()
let account = try await client.connect(issuer: "https://accounts.openvireo.com", cancel: cancel)
var step = try await account.login(
    input: LoginInput(email: email, password: Data(password.utf8), secretKey: secretKey, totp: nil, trustDevice: true),
    cancel: cancel)
while case .needsTotp(let challenge) = step {
    step = try await account.submitTotp(challenge: challenge, code: askForCode(), cancel: cancel)
}

for info in try await account.vaults(cancel: cancel) {
    print(info.name, info.role)
}
let vault = try await account.openVault(vaultId: vaultId, cancel: cancel)
let username = String(decoding: try vault.readField(reference: "ov://Personal/GitHub/username"), as: UTF8.self)
```

`secretKey` is only needed the first time on a device: after a trusted sign-in the core keeps it in the
Host's secure store. Passwords and secrets are `Data`: wipe them when you're done.

## Errors and cancelling

Every throwing call throws `OvError`. `error.code` is an `OvErrorCode` to switch on (`.unauthorized`,
`.planLimit`, `.notAvailableOffline`, …), `error.wireCode` the stable string the TypeScript SDK's `err.code`
holds, and `error.status` the HTTP status of a server error. Call `cancel.cancel()` to stop the calls that
took that token; they throw `.aborted`. A Host implementation throws `OvError(code:message:)`.
